criticism: The mint function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The increase in balance is not checked for overflow, allowing the total supply to be arbitrarily increased.
The foreignBuy function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The increase in balance is not checked for overflow, allowing the total supply to be arbitrarily increased.
The ForeignBuy function has a wrong logic vulnerability. It allows the owner to increase the balance of any user, causing a loss of funds.
The ForeignBuy function has an access control vulnerability. It can only be called by the owner, but it is public, allowing it to be called by anyone.
The ForeignBuy function has a typo in its function visibility, it is public instead of private, allowing it to be called by anyone.

The division operation in SafeMath is used incorrectly. The division operation in SafeMath is defined to return a uint256, but here it seems to be used to return a bool. This is likely a mistake. Morever, division by zero is not handled correctly. This could lead to vulnerabilities in the contract.
The mint function has an integer overflow, allowing the owner to set the balance of an arbitrary user to any value.
The unpause function does not check the caller's access rights, allowing any user to unlock the balance of the owner.
The foreignBuy function has an integer overflow, allowing the owner to set the balance of an arbitrary user to any value.
The withdraw function does not check the caller's access rights, allowing any user to access the balance of the owner.
